35647-the-canadian-portrait-gallery-volu.creator: Unknown
35647-the-canadian-portrait-gallery-volu.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Of all the many personages who have been sent over from Great Britain to administer the Government in this country, since Canada first became an appendage of the British Crown, none has achieved so wide a popularity as Lord Dufferin. None of his predecessors succeeded in creating so wide a circle of personal friends, and none has left so many pleasant remembrances behind him.

arxiv-2011-09236.title: A Multi-class Approach – Building a Visual Classifier based on Textual Descriptions using Zero-Shot Learning
arxiv-2011-09236.creator: Preeti Jagdish Sajjan, Frank G. Glavin
arxiv-2011-09236.description: Abstract Machine Learning (ML) techniques for image classification routinely require many labelled images for training the model and while testing, we ought to use images belonging to the same domain as those used for training. In this paper, we overcome the two main hurdles of ML, i.e. scarcity of data and constrained prediction of the classification model.

arxiv-2203-14992.title: Operator fusion from wavefunction overlaps: Universal finite-size corrections and application to Haagerup model
arxiv-2203-14992.creator: Yuhan Liu, Yijian Zou, Shinsei Ryu
arxiv-2203-14992.description: Abstract Given a critical quantum spin chain described by a conformal field theory (CFT) at long distances, it is crucial to understand the universal conformal data. One most important ingredient is the operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients, which describe how operators fuse into each other. It has been proposed in [Zou, Vidal, Phys. Rev.

arxiv-2205-14136.title: PSL is Dead. Long Live PSL
arxiv-2205-14136.creator: Kevin Smith, Hai Lin, Praveen Tiwari, Marjorie Sayer, Claudionor Coelho
arxiv-2205-14136.description: Abstract Property Specification Language (PSL) is a form of temporal logic that has been mainly used in discrete domains (e.g. formal hardware verification). In this paper, we show that by merging machine learning techniques with PSL monitors, we can extend PSL to work on continuous domains.

arxiv-2206-01919.title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Ransomware Detection
arxiv-2206-01919.creator: Nanda Rani, Sunita Vikrant Dhavale
arxiv-2206-01919.description: Abstract The current pandemic situation has increased cyber-attacks drastically worldwide. The attackers are using malware like trojans, spyware, rootkits, worms, ransomware heavily. Ransomware is the most notorious malware, yet we didn’t have any defensive mechanism to prevent or detect a zero-day attack. Most defensive products in the industry rely on either signature-based mechanisms or traffic-based anomalies detection.

arxiv-2207-09752.title: Close encounters: How stellar flybys shape planet-forming discs
arxiv-2207-09752.creator: Nicolás Cuello, François Ménard, Daniel J. Price
arxiv-2207-09752.description: Abstract We review the role of stellar flybys and encounters in shaping planet-forming discs around young stars, based on the published literature on this topic in the last 30 years. Since most stars ≤ 2 \leq\penalty\ 2 Myr old harbour protoplanetary discs, tidal perturbations affect planet formation.

arxiv-2209-13753.title: Light-Front Holography Model of the EMC Effect
arxiv-2209-13753.creator: Dmitriy N. Kim and Gerald A. Miller
arxiv-2209-13753.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dmitriy N. Kim and Gerald A. Miller. A new two-component model of the EMC effect based on Light-Front Holographic QCD (LFHQCD) is presented. The model suggests the EMC effect is the result of the nuclear potential breaking SU(6) symmetry.

arxiv-2310-17017.title: An Integrative Survey on Mental Health Conversational Agents to Bridge Computer Science and Medical Perspectives
arxiv-2310-17017.creator: Young-Min Cho, Sunny Rai, Lyle Ungar, João Sedoc, Sharath Chandra Guntuku
arxiv-2310-17017.description: Abstract Mental health conversational agents (a.k.a. chatbots) are widely studied for their potential to offer accessible support to those experiencing mental health challenges. Previous surveys on the topic primarily consider papers published in either computer science or medicine, leading to a divide in understanding and hindering the sharing of beneficial knowledge between both domains.

arxiv-2403-09817.title: Impact of Objective Function on Spectral Efficiency in Integrated HAPS-Terrestrial Networks
arxiv-2403-09817.creator: Afsoon Alidadi Shamsabadi 1 , Animesh Yadav 2 , and Halim Yanikomeroglu 1
arxiv-2403-09817.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Afsoon Alidadi Shamsabadi 1 , Animesh Yadav 2 , and Halim Yanikomeroglu 1. Integrating non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), in particular high altitude platform stations (HAPS), with terrestrial networks, referred to as vHetNets, emerges as a promising future wireless network architecture for providing ubiquitous connectivity. In this context, optimizing the performance of vHetNets has become a paramount concern, particularly in harmonized spectrum vHetNets, where HAPS and terrestrial networks share the same frequency band, resulting in severe inter-/intra-tier interference.

arxiv-2405-15076.title: Refined conjectures on Fitting ideals of Selmer groups over 𝐙 p 2 \mathbf{Z}_{p}^{2} -extensions
arxiv-2405-15076.creator: Cédric Dion
arxiv-2405-15076.description: Abstract . Let p > 3 p>3 be a prime number and K K be an imaginary quadratic field where p p splits. Let K ∞ K_{\infty} be the 𝐙 p 2 \mathbf{Z}_{p}^{2} -extension of K K and let K n K_{n} be a finite subextension of K ∞ / K K_{\infty}/K .

arxiv-2411-03740.title: Human-in-the-Loop Feature Selection Using Interpretable Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-based Double Deep Q-Network
arxiv-2411-03740.creator: Md Abrar Jahin 1 {}^{\textbf{1}}, \IEEEmembership Graduate Student Member, IEEE, M. F. Mridha 2 {}^{\textbf{2}}, \IEEEmembership Senior Member, IEEE, Nilanjan Dey 3 {}^{\textbf{3}}, \IEEEmembership Senior Member, IEEE and Md. Jakir Hossen 4 {}^{\textbf{4}}, \IEEEmembership Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2411-03740.description: Abstract Feature selection is critical for improving the performance and interpretability of machine learning models, particularly in high-dimensional spaces where complex feature interactions can reduce accuracy and increase computational demands. Existing approaches often rely on static feature subsets or manual intervention, limiting adaptability and scalability. However, dynamic, per-instance feature selection methods and model-specific interpretability in reinforcement learning remain underexplored.

arxiv-2411-16702.title: A Clinical Trial Design Approach to Auditing Language Models in Healthcare Setting
arxiv-2411-16702.creator: Lovedeep Gondara, Jonathan Simkin, Shebnum Devji
arxiv-2411-16702.description: Abstract We present an audit mechanism for language models, with a focus on models deployed in the healthcare setting. Our proposed mechanism takes inspiration from clinical trial design where we posit the language model audit as a single blind equivalence trial, with the comparison of interest being the subject matter experts.

arxiv-2501-13295.title: Parallel Belief Contraction via Order Aggregation
arxiv-2501-13295.creator: Jake Chandler, Richard Booth
arxiv-2501-13295.description: Abstract The standard “serial” (aka “singleton”) model of belief contraction models the manner in which an agent’s corpus of beliefs responds to the removal of a single item of information. One salient extension of this model introduces the idea of “parallel” (aka “package” or “multiple”) change, in which an entire set of items of information are simultaneously removed.

arxiv-2503-01917.title: Steer LLM Latents for Hallucination Detection
arxiv-2503-01917.creator: Seongheon Park, Xuefeng Du, Min-Hsuan Yeh, Haobo Wang, Yixuan Li
arxiv-2503-01917.description: Abstract Hallucinations in LLMs pose a significant concern to their safe deployment in real-world applications. Recent approaches have leveraged the latent space of LLMs for hallucination detection, but their embeddings, optimized for linguistic coherence rather than factual accuracy, often fail to clearly separate truthful and hallucinated content.

arxiv-2503-04226.title: Primal and Dual Characterizations for Farkas type Lemmas in Terms of Closedness Criteria
arxiv-2503-04226.creator: Dinh N, GobernaM.A, VolleM
arxiv-2503-04226.description: Abstract _This paper deals with the characterization, in terms of closedness of certain sets regarding other sets, of Farkas lemmas determining when the upperlevel set of a convex function f f contains a set of the form C ∩ 𝔸 − 1 ​ ( D ) , C\cap\mathbb{A}^{-1}\left(D\right), where C C and D D are convex sets (not necessarily cones)

arxiv-2508-18743.title: CAC-CoT: Connector-Aware Compact Chain-of-Thought for Efficient Reasoning Data Synthesis Across Dual-System Cognitive Tasks
arxiv-2508-18743.creator: Sunguk Choi, Yonghoon Kwon, Heondeuk Lee
arxiv-2508-18743.description: Abstract Long chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting helps Large Language Models (LLMs) solve difficult problems, but very long traces often slow or even degrade performance on fast, intuitive “System-1” tasks. We introduce Connector-Aware Compact CoT (CAC-CoT) — a method that deliberately restricts reasoning to a small, fixed set of connector phrases, steering the model toward concise and well — structured explanations.

arxiv-2509-02859.title: Speech DF Arena: A Leaderboard for Speech DeepFake Detection Models
arxiv-2509-02859.creator: Sandipana Dowerah 1, Atharva Kulkarni 2, Ajinkya Kulkarni 3, Hoan My Tran 4, Joonas Kalda 1, Artem Fedorchenko 1, Benoit Fauve 6, Damien Lolive 5, Tanel Alumäe 1, Matthew Magimai Doss 3 1 Tallinn University of Technology, Estonia, 2 MBZUAI, UAE, 3 Idiap Research Institute, Switzerland, 4 Univ. Renne
arxiv-2509-02859.description: Abstract Parallel to the development of advanced deepfake audio generation, audio deepfake detection has also seen significant progress. However, a standardized and comprehensive benchmark is still missing. To address this, we introduce Speech DeepFake (DF) Arena, the first comprehensive benchmark for audio deepfake detection.

europmc-pmc10478756.title: Cardiovascular complications in chronic kidney disease: a review from the European Renal and Cardiovascular Medicine Working Group of the European Renal Association.
europmc-pmc10478756.creator: Zoccali C, Mallamaci F, Adamczak M, de Oliveira RB, Massy ZA, Sarafidis P, Agarwal R, Mark PB, Kotanko P, Ferro CJ, Wanner C, Burnier M, Vanholder R, Wiecek A.
europmc-pmc10478756.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is classified into five stages with kidney failure being the most severe stage (stage G5). CKD conveys a high risk for coronary artery disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Cardiovascular complications are the most common...

pmc-10535609.title: Simultaneous Extraction and Determination of Lignans from Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. via Diol-Based Matrix Solid-Phase Dispersion with High-Performance Liquid Chromatography
pmc-10535609.creator: Yinpeng Wang, Jingbo Zhu, Xinxin Du, Yumei Li, Giovanni D’Orazio
pmc-10535609.description: The quality of Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. (S. chinensis) is principally attributed to lignan compounds. In this paper, a simple and rapid strategy for simultaneous extraction and determination of 10 lignans from S. chinensis was established through matrix solid-phase dispersion (MSPD) assisted by diol-functionalized silica (Diol). The experimental parameters for MSPD extraction were screened using the response surface methodology (RSM).

pmc-11402043.title: Previously unrecognized and potentially consequential challenges facing Hsp90 inhibitors in cancer clinical trials
pmc-11402043.creator: Cheng Chang, Xin Tang, David T Woodley, Mei Chen, Wei Li
pmc-11402043.description: Targeting the heat shock protein-90 (Hsp90) chaperone machinery in various cancers with 200 monotherapy or combined-therapy clinical trials since 1999 has not yielded any success of food and drug administration approval. Blames for the failures were unanimously directed at the Hsp90 inhibitors or tumors or both.

pmc-11605619.title: 10010- NI-1 QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF RECURRENCE PATTERNS AND DIRECTIONALITY IN PRIMARY GLIOBLASTOMA USING LESION MAPS & TRACTOGRAPHY
pmc-11605619.creator: Takeshi Shimizu, Hirotaka Satoh, Takahiro Sanada, Masato Saitou, Nobuyuki Mitsui, Satoru Hiroshima, Manabu Kinoshita
pmc-11605619.description: INTRODUCTIONIdentifying the sites of recurrence in primary glioblastoma is crucial for developing aggressive initial treatments. This study focuses on glioblastoma originating in the frontal lobe, hypothesizing that “recurrence progression is related to nerve fiber trajectories.” We quantitatively examined recurrence patterns. METHODSWe analyzed 30 cases of primary glioblastoma in the frontal lobe treated at our institution with confirmed recurrences.

pmc-11610932.title: Notch induces transcription by stimulating release of paused RNA polymerase II
pmc-11610932.creator: Julia M Rogers, Claudia A Mimoso, Benjamin JE Martin, Alexandre P Martin, Jon C Aster, Karen Adelman, Stephen C Blacklow
pmc-11610932.description: In this study, using high-resolution genomic assays of chromatin accessibility and nascent RNA production, Rogers et al. comprehensively examined the response to human Notch1 across a time course of activation to investigate how Notch activates transcription of its target genes.

pmc-12984302.title: Validity and Reliability of the Turkish Version of the Temporomandibular Joint Ankylosis Quality of Life Questionnaire (TMJAQoL-TR) in Patients with Severe Temporomandibular Disorders
pmc-12984302.creator: Manolya İlhanli, Mehmet Alptekin Karaçeşme, Kaan Gündüz, Mahmut Yaran, İlker İlhanli
pmc-12984302.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: The Temporomandibular Joint Ankylosis Quality of Life Questionnaire (TMJAQoL) is a disease-specific instrument designed to assess quality of life in patients with temporomandibular joint (TMJ) ankylosis. No validated Turkish version of this scale existed prior to this study. The aim of this study was to translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the Turkish version of the TMJAQoL (TMJAQoL-TR) in patients with severe temporomandibular disorders, including a predefined ankylosis subgroup. Materials and Methods: A total of 120 patients with temporomandibular complaints were included.

pmc-13012215.title: Distinct neuroinflammatory profiles in progressive supranuclear palsy associated with HLA haplotypes
pmc-13012215.creator: Shelley L Forrest, Sarah S Zaheer, Ain Kim, Hidetomo Tanaka, Helen Chasiotis, Jun Li, Susan H Fox, Jinguo Wang, M Carmela Tartaglia, Anthony E Lang, Gabor G Kovacs
pmc-13012215.description: Progressive supranuclear palsy is a neurodegenerative four-repeat tauopathy characterized by atypical parkinsonism and cognitive behavioural changes and a relatively uniform neuropathology. Building on prior identification of rare HLA (human leukocyte antigen) haplotypes in progressive supranuclear palsy, this study investigates whether these haplotypes correlate with distinct clinical and immunopathological phenotypes.

pmc-13553112.title: Cigarette smoke and e-cigarette aerosol extracts induce myelopoiesis and suppress inflammatory cytokine production
pmc-13553112.creator: Jeanette Y C Sullivan, Helen X Huang, Jianhong C Heidmann, Francisco Diaz, Camille Brzechffa, Jane H Chen, Eli M Soyfer, Nneamaka Iwobi, Irene Hasen, Amanda Ting, Nicole Sparks, Michael T Kleinman, Angela G Fleischman
pmc-13553112.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Tobacco and nicotine use remain leading preventable drivers of cancer risk, and both combustible cigarettes and electronic nicotine devices perturb immune function and hematopoiesis. However, side-by-side comparisons of their effects across the hematopoietic hierarchy remain limited. Here, we evaluate the impact of cigarette smoke extract (CSE) and e-cigarette vapor extract (EVE) on inflammatory responses in mature myeloid cells and on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell function using complementary in vitro and in vivo approaches.

pmc-13591293.title: CNTN5 Promotes Invasion and Metastasis in Non‐Small Cell Lung Cancer by Regulating YAP1 Nuclear Translocation
pmc-13591293.creator: Jiarui Wang, Mengtao Wang, Yanze Yin, Ao Zeng, Keyi Chen, Zhilong Xu, Jie Dai
pmc-13591293.description: BackgroundNon‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a leading cause of cancer‐related death worldwide, largely owing to its high metastatic potential. Contactin‐5 (CNTN5), a glycosylphosphatidylinositol‐anchored membrane protein, has been implicated in tumor‐related processes; however, its role in NSCLC progression remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the clinical relevance, biological function, and underlying mechanism of CNTN5 in NSCLC.
